brief:
# Glossary + Index + Demonstration Designer (Brett)

## 1. Encyclopedia-grade glossary & index
Build a complete glossary AND index of EVERYTHING in the system — as thorough as indexing an encyclopedia. Cover every plugin, feature, UI element, setting, preference, ability, function, asset, chain, document, command, API/MCP/CLI tool, hook, and the smallest items.
- Walk every plugin meticulously and document everything it does.
- For every asset and element: a detailed summary of what it is, what it does, how it works, what it links to / depends on, where it appears, its scope and inheritance, its context menu, and its API.
- Two structured outputs: a Glossary (defined terms, searchable, cross-linked) and an Index (hierarchical, categorized, like a book index) — both sortable, filterable, searchable, multi-view.
- Source it from the UI registry + plugin manifests so it stays complete and current automatically; add a CI check that flags any registered asset/feature missing an entry.

## 2. Demonstration Designer (off the walkthrough system)
- From ANY glossary/index entry, click 'Generate demonstration' to produce a walkthrough/demo of that feature using the existing walkthrough engine.
- Demonstrations are assets: editable, replayable, voice-controlled, can be chained into larger tours.
- The Demonstration Designer lets you assemble/edit demos (steps, narration, highlights, actions) and run them against the live UI or a target preview surface.

## Rules
- Everything is registry assets; full voice + API/MCP/CLI parity.
- Settings in categorized collapsible sections.
- Submit at least 3 UI options to UI Review first.
## Addendum 1 — Book Builder (Brett)
Go beyond single demos: author full BOOKS (like writing a book, similar model to the to-do list).
- 'Create new book' -> wizard: rough total length, length per chapter, style, theme, narrator voice, and other options.
- Chapters: create and organize chapters. Multiple books live in a collapsible tree; drag items to the exact spot in a book. Reorder via drag, context menu, or the icons on top of columns/windows/containers.
- Content picker: browse EVERYTHING in the glossary/index via filtered, sortable trees and grids with multiple view types; drag entries into a book/chapter.
- Per-book you can set how much time is dedicated to it (and per chapter).
- Live sandbox preview: selecting a UI/feature/glossary/index entry opens a floating window showing a REAL, sandboxed version of that thing with real data — the actual focus of that part of the book.
- Preview the whole book, then Generate a walkthrough video (narrated, themed) and other outputs.
- Books, chapters and demos are all assets; voice + API/MCP/CLI parity; built on the existing walkthrough engine.

## Addendum 2 — Interactive documentation output for books (Brett)
When building a book, checkboxes choose whether to also generate DOCUMENTATION, what type, and how extensive (from light up to extremely deep). The top tier is full-blown interactive HTML + TypeScript documentation: real, runnable, interactive examples, live/interactive components throughout, deep and hardcore — the real deal, not static pages. Documentation is generated alongside the book/walkthrough from the same sources (glossary/index/registry + sandbox), kept in sync, and saved as an asset. Options for depth, format, and how interactive. Voice + API/MCP/CLI parity.

## Addendum 3 — Orchestrator auto-updates the catalog on every future build (Brett)
Make catalog upkeep automatic and permanent. From now on, whenever ANY build is created/lands, the orchestrator updates this glossary + index + catalog: add/update entries for every new or changed plugin, feature, asset, setting, function, chain, document, etc., sourced from the registry + plugin manifests. Keep it complete and current with no manual step. Add it to the build lifecycle (part of the standard post-build hook) and write the rule into RULES.md / the brief template so every build does it. CI check fails if a registered asset/feature has no catalog entry after a build.

## Addendum 4 — Generated clips are auto-tagged registry assets (Brett)
Every clip/demo/walkthrough/video generated by this system automatically gets a large set of keywords/tags attached (from the source glossary/index entry, plugin, assets shown, actions, topics — auto-extracted), and is itself registered as an asset in the registry. So every generated clip is: a first-class registry asset (id, kind=clip/demo), richly keyword-tagged, searchable/filterable/sortable like everything else, and reusable (droppable into books, chainable). Voice + API/MCP/CLI parity.
